content: 1. The report titled Trends in Maternal Mortality: 2000 to 2017, published by WHO, UNICEF, UNFPA, the World Bank Group, and the United Nations Population Division, provides comprehensive estimates of maternal mortality trends over a 17-year period. This document was accessed on July 9, 2020. 2. Say et al. conducted a systematic analysis of global causes of maternal death, published in The Lancet Global Health in 2014. This study highlights the primary contributors to maternal mortality worldwide, emphasizing the need for targeted interventions. 3. The 2019 Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) report outlines progress and challenges in achieving global health targets, including maternal health. This report was accessed on July 9, 2020. 4. The Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights issued technical guidance on applying a human rights-based approach to policies aimed at reducing preventable maternal morbidity and mortality. This guidance was accessed on July 9, 2020. 5. Tuncalp et al. presented the WHO vision for improving the quality of care for pregnant women and newborns in a 2015 publication in BJOG. The study emphasizes the importance of evidence-based practices to enhance maternal and neonatal outcomes. 6. A joint statement by WHO, UNFPA, UNICEF, ICM, ICN, FIGO, and IPA in 2018 defined the competencies required for skilled health personnel providing care during childbirth. This statement was accessed on July 9, 2020. 7. Carroli et al. conducted a systematic review on the epidemiology of postpartum hemorrhage, published in Best Practice & Research Clinical Obstetrics & Gynaecology in 2008. The study provides critical insights into the prevalence, risk factors, and management of this condition. 8. Souza et al. explored the effectiveness of essential interventions for reducing maternal mortality in the WHO Multi-Country Survey on Maternal and Newborn Health. This cross-sectional study was published in The Lancet in 2013. 9. Oyelese and Ananth reviewed the epidemiology, risk factors, and causes of postpartum hemorrhage in a 2010 article in Clinical Obstetrics and Gynecology. The study underscores the importance of early identification and management of this life-threatening condition. 10. Daru et al. conducted a multilevel analysis on the risk of maternal mortality in women with severe anemia during pregnancy and postpartum. This study, published in The Lancet Global Health in 2018, highlights the critical need for addressing anemia in maternal health programs. 11. Weeks AD reviewed the retained placenta in a 2008 article in Best Practice & Research Clinical Obstetrics & Gynaecology. The study discusses the etiology, risk factors, and management strategies for this obstetric complication. 12. Weeks et al. conducted a double-blind, randomized controlled trial on the use of umbilical vein oxytocin for treating retained placenta (the Release Study). This trial, published in The Lancet in 2010, evaluates the efficacy of this intervention compared to expectant management. 13. The WHO Executive Guideline Steering Group developed updated recommendations for maternal and perinatal health, emphasizing evidence-based practices to improve outcomes. This document was accessed on July 9, 2020. 14. Vogel et al. described the development and application of a living guidelines approach to WHO recommendations on maternal and perinatal health in a 2019 article in BMJ Global Health. This approach ensures that guidelines remain current and relevant. 15. The second edition of the WHO Handbook for Guideline Development provides a systematic framework for creating evidence-based health recommendations. This resource was accessed on July 9, 2020. 16. WHO recommendations for the prevention and treatment of postpartum hemorrhage outline evidence-based strategies to reduce maternal morbidity and mortality. This guideline was accessed on July 9, 2020. 17. Finlayson et al. conducted a qualitative systematic review to identify what matters most to women and healthcare providers regarding interventions for preventing postpartum hemorrhage. This study was published in PLOS One in 2019. 18. Meher et al. developed core outcome sets for the prevention and treatment of postpartum hemorrhage through an international Delphi consensus study. This work was published in BJOG in 2019. 19. Nardin et al. reviewed the use of umbilical vein injection for managing retained placenta in a Cochrane systematic review published in 2011. The study evaluates the clinical feasibility and effectiveness of this technique. 20. Alonso-Coello et al. introduced the GRADE Evidence to Decision (EtD) frameworks in a 2016 article in BMJ. This systematic approach facilitates well-informed healthcare decision-making. 21. Downe et al. conducted a systematic qualitative review on what matters to women during childbirth, published in PLOS One in 2018. The study highlights the importance of patient-centered care in maternal health. 22. Lewin et al. described the application of GRADE-CERQual to qualitative evidence synthesis findings in a 2018 article in Implementation Science. This methodology ensures the reliability and transparency of qualitative research. 23. Pipingas et al. conducted a clinical feasibility study on a new technique for umbilical vein injection to manage retained placenta, published in the East African Medical Journal in 1994. 24. WHO standards for improving the quality of maternal and newborn care in health facilities provide a framework for enhancing care delivery. This document was accessed on August 6, 2020.
